investigations.name: cbc-01-cxx-reference-baseline
investigations.description:
This study exists because the expert asked for a careful comparison against existing Chaste
results, and chose regenerated C++ output over published figures as the reference.

The critical trap is documented in the authors' own source: every test file ships with the
paper parameters COMMENTED OUT and short continuous-integration values active. For cell
sorting, M_TIME_FOR_SIMULATION is 11.0 in the repo versus 100 in the paper. Running the
suite as-cloned produces a plausible-looking but wrong baseline — the single highest-risk
silent failure in this investigation. Restoring those blocks is step one, and the diff must
be recorded.

The build is the other risk. The project's CMakeLists declares
find_package(Chaste COMPONENTS cell_based crypt), so the crypt component must be built even
though the sorting case study does not use it. The paper pins historical Chaste branches
(paper/CellBasedComparison, paper/CellBasedComparison18) against Oxford servers that are no
longer the live mirror; we build against the GitHub mirror's develop and record the commit.

Output lands in $CHASTE_TEST_OUTPUT/CellSorting/{Ca,Potts,Node,Mesh,Vertex}. The measure the
investigation turns on is heterotypicboundary.dat, whose four columns are
(heterotypic_boundary_length, total_shared_edges_length, num_heterotypic_pairs,
total_num_pairs). The paper's fractional boundary length is column 1 / column 2 — the writer
does NOT divide, so the reduction is ours to perform and to test.

investigations.name: cbc-02-onlattice-wrapper-extension
investigations.description:
The current wrapper is a 12-combination demo of a single simulation class. Three structural
changes are needed, and the first is the one that breaks the existing design.

(1) OnLatticeSimulation. `_chaste_server.py` hardcodes OffLatticeSimulation2_2, and the
force/_apply_stiffness abstraction does not generalise: on-lattice populations take update
rules via AddUpdateRule, not forces via AddForce. This needs a real dispatch seam, not another
branch in the existing if-chain.

(2) Ghost nodes for VT. The paper's VT is MeshBasedCellPopulationWithGhostNodes with 20 ghost
layers; the wrapper's `mesh` population calls HoneycombMeshGenerator(w, h) with no ghost
argument and is therefore NOT the paper's VT. The output extractor also assumes every location
index is a real cell, so it must learn to filter GetGhostNodeIndices — otherwise ghosts are
silently counted as cells and every population-level number is wrong.

(3) Two cell types. The paper relaxes to steady state, then labels ~50% of cells with CellLabel
and runs on. The wrapper has no notion of cell type or labelling at all.

Scope note: CA is deliberately excluded. Its DifferentialAdhesionCaSwitchingUpdateRule is custom
to the paper's repo, and AbstractCaSwitchingUpdateRule_2 exposes no constructor to subclass —
see the investigation's decisions_needed. CaBasedCellPopulation itself IS bound, so the CA
population may still be constructed; only its adhesion-driven switching is out of reach.

Two landmines from the existing code carry over: every Chaste object must be retained in _KEEP
or the next call aborts with "pure virtual method called", and state must be extracted before
any teardown because TearDownNotebookTest segfaults after a real run.

investigations.name: cbc-03-random-motion-equivalence
investigations.description:
PyChaste cannot express the paper's RandomMotionForce. The probe established that Chaste's
abstract bases, while reachable via MRO (AbstractForce_2_2), cannot carry a working Python
subclass in this image: the C++ -> Python trampoline fails marshalling the population argument
("Unable to convert std::shared_ptr<T> to Python when the bound type does not use
std::shared_ptr or py::smart_holder as its holder type"). This reproduces with an override that
never touches its argument, while an identical mainline-only control solves — so it is the
binding layer, not user code. Since OS, VT and VM sorting all need random motion, the whole
reproduction rests on finding a mainline substitute.

Reading both sources side by side, the force laws are the same expression:

  RandomMotionForce:  F = sqrt(2 * mMovementParameter * dt) / dt * xi
  DiffusionForce:     F = nu * sqrt(2 * (scaling / node_radius) * dt) / dt * xi

Both draw xi from StandardNormalRandomDeviate per dimension, both iterate rGetMesh() nodes, and
both scale by dt so the discretised update gives x_new = x_old + sqrt(2*D*dt)*W. They coincide
when nu = 1 and scaling / node_radius = mMovementParameter. Chaste's default damping constant is
1.0, and the paper sets eta = 1.0 for OS and VT — so nu = 1 is the paper's own regime, not a
convenient assumption.

Three ways this could still be wrong, which is what the study is for:

- DiffusionForce THROWS if any node radius is 0, and 0 is the default for vertex meshes. VM and
  VT need radii set on every node. Whether setting a radius on a vertex-mesh node perturbs
  anything else is untested.
- nu comes from GetDampingConstant(node_index), which is per-node and could diverge from 1.0 for
  labelled cells or under a mutation state, silently rescaling the noise.
- The two forces consume random numbers from the same global generator. Even with identical
  force laws, differing call ORDER or COUNT desynchronises the stream, so per-seed trajectories
  will not match step-for-step even when the distributions do. The comparison must therefore be
  distributional over many seeds, not trajectory-identical — mistaking this for a real
  divergence is the likely false alarm.

investigations.name: cbc-04-cell-sorting-reproduction
investigations.description:
The payoff study. It runs the same protocol as cbc-01 but through pbg-chaste's PyChaste wrapper,
and the comparison between the two is the investigation's actual result.

Protocol, per the authors' code: a 20x20 tissue of non-dividing DifferentiatedCellProliferativeType
cells relaxes to steady state to t = 10; ~50% are then labelled with CellLabel; the simulation
runs a further 100 h. Per model, from the authors' source rather than the paper's tables:

- CP: PottsMeshGenerator(240,20,4,240,20,4), OnLatticeSimulation, dt 0.01, temperature 0.2,
  VolumeConstraintPottsUpdateRule(16, 0.1), SurfaceAreaConstraintPottsUpdateRule(16, 0.01),
  DifferentialAdhesionPottsUpdateRule(0.1/0.5/0.1/0.2/1.0). All mainline.
- OS: HoneycombMeshGenerator(20,20,0) -> NodesOnlyMesh cutoff 2.5, OffLatticeSimulation, dt 1/200,
  DifferentialAdhesionGeneralisedLinearSpringForce (stiffness 50, homotypic x1.0, heterotypic
  x0.1, cutoff 2.5) + random motion 0.05.
- VT: HoneycombMeshGenerator(20,20,20 ghosts) -> MeshBasedCellPopulationWithGhostNodes, same
  force at default cutoff 1.5, + random motion 0.1.
- VM: HoneycombVertexMeshGenerator(20,20), rearrangement threshold 0.1,
  NagaiHondaDifferentialAdhesionForce(50/1.0/1.0/2.0/1.0/10.0/20.0) + random motion 0.1. Note the
  authors set CellData "target area" = 1.0 per cell BY HAND and deliberately do NOT attach
  SimpleTargetAreaModifier, with a source comment that the modifiers misbehave by producing very
  long G1 phases. Reproduce their choice, not the idiomatic one.

Random motion in OS/VT/VM comes from DiffusionForce configured per cbc-03. That substitution is
this study's central dependency and its most likely source of divergence — which is precisely
why cbc-03 gates it.

CA is out of scope: blocked on the custom DifferentialAdhesionCaSwitchingUpdateRule. Report it as
a binding-coverage finding with the probe evidence, not as a simulation result, and do not quietly
drop it from the model list — an unexplained 4-model figure against a 5-model paper reads as an
omission rather than a finding.

Feasibility: 4 models x 10 seeds x 100 h at 20x20 under amd64 emulation is likely infeasible on
this laptop. Size the runs before committing, and move to the Mac mini if needed. The Fig 3
k_pert sweep (9 values) is a stretch goal and should not gate the headline comparison.
